name: A shared folder
description: Files and folders on a network share, SFTP server or mounted drive.

objects.label: files
objects.description: Files in a folder and the folders below it.

fields.label: subfolder
fields.description: The path below the folder named above, such as Invoices/2026.

fields.label: type
fields.description: Worked out from the file extension.

fields.label: owner
fields.description: Who created or last saved the file. Not every share records this.

objects.label: folders
objects.description: The folders directly inside a folder.

fields.label: last modified
fields.description: When something inside it last changed.

actions.label: a file
actions.description: Writes the result as one file. Choose a format the next reader can open.

params.label: named
params.description: Leave empty to name it after the source and the date.

actions.label: the files
actions.description: Moves each file in the source. Files disappear from where they were.

params.label: if a file with that name exists

actions.label: a new folder
actions.description: One folder per record, for example a folder per new client or project.

guidance: A shared folder is a Windows (SMB) share, an SFTP server or a drive mounted on the machine the automation runs on, and it is reached with a service account that has its own permissions on the share. Paths and file names should be spelled exactly, with the drive letter or UNC path the server uses rather than the one on someone's laptop, and a file that is still being written can be picked up half-finished, so wait until it has stopped changing. Ask for read access to the source folders and write access only to the destination folder; never run as a person's account.

setup.notes: The IT or systems team can create a service account and grant it access to the named folders. Tell them which folders are read and which are written.
